comment: One row for each gen rule, kill rule and definition of the emptiness pass, the static
overwrite check of D17.11 (src/fort/fir/emptiness.ft), for its report in a build, under
--check and under --fir, and for the proof that the build-mode pass reads
(src/fort/fir_passes.ft). A row names the line that decides the rule and a text that breaks
it. The first stage runs the cases over FIR text and the examples over fort source
(test/fort/fir/emptiness_test.ft). The second runs the build-mode suite
(test/fort/fir_passes_test.ft). The third runs the driver test, which holds the error in
each mode. The fourth holds each program that stopped at run time before the rule became
static against the error at its old site (test/overwrite_oracle_test.py). The table runs in
the Linux VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the product
compiler, whose driver and emitter import fir.emptiness.

stages.name: the emptiness module test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 fir/emptiness

stages.name: the build-mode suite
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 fir_passes_test

stages.name: the driver test
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 driver_test
